summary: Mars Ramani is a live, interactive web platform for planning astronaut spacewalks on Mars, built entirely on NASA data and focused on Jezero Crater, Arcadia Planitia and Deuteronilus Mensae. Existing planetary mapping tools offer broad orbital views or raw archives that are hard to use and rarely combine the hazards that matter to someone on foot. Mars Ramani brings NASA’s orbital imagery, elevation data, Perseverance mission records, Curiosity radiation measurements, live solar-storm alerts and subsurface-ice maps into one place. Users explore 24 science locations in real 360° panoramas and follow routes that trace the path Perseverance drove, with distance, climb, difficulty and the nearest shelter for every leg, alongside hazards, radiation and dust-storm season. Every value is labelled measured, derived, modelled or unavailable, so planners know what to trust. It matters because crews, researchers and students can answer Where am I? Is it safe? Where can I shelter? without parsing raw archives by hand, and an offline mode lets schools without full equipment teach astronaut skills. It is a planning prototype, not certified navigation software.
details: Google Earth shows you a place. Martian Map tells an astronaut whether to go there. Our Interplanetary Survival Guide is a Street View–style planning tool built entirely on NASA data, covering Jezero Crater plus two water-ice sites, Arcadia Planitia and Deuteronilus Mensae. Astronauts explore 24 science locations through real 360° panoramas, following proven ground: routes trace the path Perseverance actually drove, each leg showing distance, climb, difficulty and nearest shelter. Survival, not sightseeing: a safety panel combines dust-storm season, Curiosity’s radiation data, live NASA solar-storm alerts, mapped hazards and shelters where terrain blocks the most sky. Honesty makes it valid: every value is tagged measured, derived, modelled or unavailable, gaps read “Data unavailable,” and the Cheyava Falls biosignature is labelled unconfirmed, which is rare in a hackathon demo. It also works offline, so schools without full equipment can teach students about astronauts and the skills of the profession. Built with TypeScript, Python, React, Leaflet, Pannellum, rasterio and NumPy, with 46 automated tests, on a laptop with Claude’s help. We weighed safety, science goals, planetary protection and honesty, aiming to help crews balance science against risk and inspire the public. It is a planning prototype, not certified navigation software.
